belief: Since the world is ending, planning for the future doesn’t matter.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that since the world is ending planning for the future doesn’t matter, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching that the end is so near that education, savings, or careers are pointless. Discouragement or hopelessness about the world. Using the end times as a reason to avoid responsibility. Past predictions that led people to quit jobs or sell homes. Feeling that only “spiritual” activities matter.
teaches: Christ will return, but no one knows when. Until then, Scripture calls us to faithful, ordinary lives. In Jesus’ parable, the master told his servants, “Conduct business with this until I return.” Paul told believers to live quietly and work with their hands, and he corrected those who stopped working because they expected the end. God told exiles to build houses, plant gardens, and seek the good of their city. Our labor in the Lord is not in vain.
self_statements: Why plan when the world is ending?
Education and careers don’t matter anymore.
I don’t need to take care of my health or future.
Only spiritual things are worth doing now.
There’s no point in starting anything long-term.
errors: Assuming you know the end is too close to plan.
Using the end times as a reason to avoid responsibility.
Overlooking commands to work faithfully until Christ returns.
questions: What did the master tell his servants to do until he returned?
What did Paul tell believers who stopped working?
What did God tell the exiles in Babylon to do?
Does Scripture say my labor is in vain?
Who would be affected if I stopped planning: my family, my future self?
Is this belief helping me be faithful or helping me avoid something?
What faithful plan could I make this week?
truth: Planning for the future still matters. Jesus will return, but until then He calls me to be faithful with what He has given me. Work, savings, education, health, and relationships are part of faithful living. My labor in the Lord is not in vain, and I can plan wisely while trusting God with the timing.
hw_questions: What did the master tell his servants?
What did Paul tell those who stopped working?
What did God tell the exiles?
Who would be affected if I stopped planning?
What faithful plan could I make this week?
hw_truths: Jesus calls me to be faithful until He returns.
Planning wisely is part of faithful living.
My labor in the Lord is not in vain.
I can seek the good of the place where I live.
I can work, save, and grow while trusting God.
God holds the timing; I hold today’s responsibilities.
log: Each day, write one responsible step I took for my future or my family.
name_example: Therefore, Sarah, be steadfast and immovable. Always excel in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
actions: Make one practical plan this week:
a budget, a savings goal, a class, or a health appointment.
and write what the faithful servants did while their master was away.
and write one way you can seek the good of your community.
about balancing hope in Christ’s return with planning.
tracker: One responsible step for my future
prayer: Father, thank You for the hope of Christ’s return. Help me reject the lie that planning for the future doesn’t matter because the world is ending. Make me a faithful steward of my time, work, money, and relationships until Jesus comes. In His name, Amen.
